native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28.0 pages (n=18) and that in Psychology is 11.2 pages (n=97); thus Experimental Economics original papers are on average markedly longer (~2.5x) than Psychology original papers.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected both CSVs; only meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927x57) contains required fields length/project/discipline (the replication_success CSV lacks them). 2) Grouping by project: Experimental Economics = project=='ee' (18 papers, coincides exactly with discipline=='Economics'); Psychology = project=='rpp' (97 papers, Social 55 + Cognitive 42). The discipline field has no 'Psychology' category, so project is the only operational grouping matching the question. 3) Unit of analysis = each original paper: deduplicated by id (927 rows -> 141 unique papers; duplication only in ml1/ml3, not in ee/rpp). 4) Verified length has 0 missing values (927/927), no imputation needed. 5) Computed per-group mean, SD, median, min, max of length at study level and confirmed row-level vs study-level means are identical for ee/rpp. 6) Final result: ee mean=28.0 pages (n=18, sd=7.37, median=27.5); rpp mean=11.2 pages (n=97, sd=6.30, median=9.0).
